analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Well, not entirely. I don't eat meat at all, but I don't have a problem eating fish, seafood or eggs. 嗯，不完全是。我完全不吃肉，但吃鱼、海鲜或蛋是没问题的。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 被问者应答 + not entirely 让步 + but 转折。男士问 you're not vegetarian, are you?， 女士的应答即落点；她先说 not entirely（不完全是），再用 but 把「不吃肉」和「吃鱼 蛋」对接——这种「部分是、不完全是」正是 partial vegetarian 的定义。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: I don't eat meat at all, but I don't have a problem eating fish, seafood or eggs ↔ She is a partial vegetarian. 「不吃肉但吃鱼蛋」概括为「部分素食者」 not entirely ↔partial vegetarian 「不完全是」对应「部分」

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 与原文相反 She eats meat occasionally.（偶尔吃肉）与原文 I don't eat meat at all（完全不吃肉） 正好相反，把「一点都不吃」反成了「偶尔吃」。 借用原文：I don't eat meat at all B) 张冠李戴 She enjoys cheeseburgers. 盗用了男士那句 bacon cheeseburgers，但说舍不得汉堡的 是男士、不是女士，把男方的话安到了女方头上。 借用原文：bacon cheeseburgers C) 原词陷阱 She is allergic to seafood. 盗用了 seafood 一词，但原文是她「吃海鲜没问题」，根本没 提过敏，allergic 系凭空捏造且与事实相反。 借用原文：eating fish, seafood or eggs

questions.stem: What does the woman say about her parents?
questions.stemZh: 这位女士关于她父母说了什么?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Both are in their 70s now, but eat organic as often as possible and take part in regular physical exercise. Neither of them has any health problems, and they hardly ever get sick. 他们俩现在都七十多岁了，但尽量常吃有机食品，也定期参加体育锻炼。两人都没有任何健 康问题，也几乎从不生病。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 强否定 Neither…any + hardly ever 收束健康结论。落点在 Neither of them has any health problems 与 they hardly ever get sick——双重否定 + hardly ever 把父母身体状 况推到「完全没病、几乎不生病」的极佳状态，这是对父母的总体定论。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: Neither of them has any health problems, and they hardly ever get sick ↔ They enjoy perfect health. 「都没病、几乎不生病」=「身体极佳」

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: B) 与原文相反 They are both animal lovers. 借了 animal preservation 一词，但原文说父母 not terribly active or knowledgeable about animal preservation efforts（对动物保护既不 热心也不懂），与「都是爱动物者」相反。 借用原文：not terribly active or knowledgeable about animal preservation efforts C) 偷换概念 They only eat organic food. 盗用 eat organic，却把原文的 as often as possible（尽量 常吃）偷改成 only（只吃），范围被绝对化，不符。 借用原文：eat organic as often as possible D) 张冠李戴 They are cutting back on coffee. 盗用了 cutting back on coffee，但戒咖啡的是女士自 己（I tried cutting back on coffee），父母从未减咖啡，把女士的事安到了父母身上。 借用原文：I tried cutting back on coffee 1 W: How did your annual performance evaluation meeting with your manager go? Did you get much in the way of praise? W: 你和经理的年度绩效评估会谈怎么样?他有没有表扬你? 2 M: Next to zero. When we came to the part about discussing my areas for growth, he bluntly told me that I had an attitude problem. But he wouldn't really expand on that description. He said it's the little things I do and say. M: 几乎没有。当我们谈到需要改进的地方时,他直截了当地说我有态度问题。但他没有详细说明。他说是 我做的和说的一些小事。 3 W: Did you ask him for a specific example? W: 你有没有让他举个具体例子? 4 M: I did ask him a few more questions to try and narrow it down. He said my constant questioning of him and his decisions was the most obvious example he could give. Then our conversation was swiftly brought to a close. M: 我确实又问了他几个问题,想把范围缩小一点。他说我不断质疑他和他的决定是他能给出的最明显的例 子。然后我们的对话就迅速结束了。 5 W: I had a similar experience once. My manager told me I was too honest. In most cases, I thought my honesty was helpful, as did my colleagues, but my manager thought otherwise. Some managers really adopt manipulative language to disguise the unreasonable choices they have made. They don't use the rational power of arguments to resolve issues of conflict or complaints about unfairness. W: 我有过类似的经历。我的经理说我太诚实了。在大多数情况下,我觉得我的诚实是有帮助的,我的同事也 这么认为,但我的经理不这么想。有些经理真的会采用操控性的语言来掩饰他们做出的不合理选择。他们不 用理性论证的力量来解决冲突问题或关于不公平的投诉。 Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard. 6 M: Right. Some employ their persuasive vocabulary and influential communication style to win workplace arguments by compelling people to perform the intended action. M: 没错。有些人运用他们的说服性词汇和有影响力的沟通风格,通过迫使人们执行预定行动来赢得职场 争论。 7 W: Exactly. Too honest? Isn't that a good thing? I thought that's surely something we should have covered earlier in the section discussing strengths and talents, but no. Honesty was deemed to be more of a sin than a virtue, since it made people feel uncomfortable, or at least it made the most powerful folks feel uncomfortable. W: 就是这样。太诚实?这难道不是件好事吗?我觉得这肯定应该在前面讨论优势和才能的部分提到,但没 有。诚实被认为更像是一种罪过而不是美德,因为它让人感到不舒服,或者至少让那些最有权势的人感到不 舒服。 8 M: Indeed. Rhetoric is viewed by many philosophers as the method through which the powerful accumulate more power. By virtue of having the loudest voice, they're able to command greater attention and to further assert their dominance, even when what they're saying doesn't really make much sense. M: 确实如此。许多哲学家认为修辞是权势者积累更多权力的方法。凭借最响亮的声音,他们能够获得更多 关注,并进一步巩固自己的支配地位,即使他们说的话并没有多大意义。 9 W: And retaining their power and prestige is their priority. W: 保持权力和威望是他们的首要任务。 10 M: It's what makes the most sense to a lot of them. M: 这对他们很多人来说是最合理的。

questions.answerText: They use manipulative language to mask their irrational choices.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Some managers really adopt manipulative language to disguise the unreasonable choices they have made. 有些经理确实会采用操控性的语言，来掩饰他们做出的那些不合理的选择。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 女士发言中直接评价经理的核心陈述句。女士这段以 Some managers really adopt manipulative language to disguise the unreasonable choices 直陈对经理的判断，主语 Some managers、动词 adopt…to disguise 把'手段+目的'说全，是承载答案的评价句。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: adopt manipulative language ↔use manipulative language adopt 换成 use，同义动词替换 disguise the unreasonable choices ↔mask their irrational choices disguise→mask、unreasonable→irrational 双重同义替换

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 答非所问 原文批评的是经理'用话术掩盖不合理决定'，重点在'掩盖'这个语言行为；A 的 make unhelpful decisions for solving problems 只截取'决定不好'一层，丢了'操控语言'的核 心，且 unhelpful 与原文 unreasonable 侧重不同，未答到点上。 借用原文：disguise the unreasonable choices they have made B) 未提及 原文没说经理 favor some employees' suggestions over others'偏心采纳某些建议'，这 是凭'经理不公'的印象自造的指控，原文无对应句。 D) 原词陷阱 原文紧接的下一句是 They don't use the rational power of arguments to resolve issues'他们不用理性论证去解决问题'，D 的 reject employees' reasonable arguments for work efficiency 盗用 rational/arguments 这两个原词，并自添 for work efficiency(为 了效率)的动机，原文既没说'否决员工合理论点'，更没提'效率'，原词在意思被改向。 借用原文：They don't use the rational power of arguments to resolve issues of conflict

analysis.text: Honesty was deemed to be more of a sin than a virtue, since it made people feel uncomfortable. 诚实被认为更像是一种罪过而非美德，因为它让人感到不舒服。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 评价动词 deemed 引出的定性，是态度落点。女士用 Honesty was deemed to be more of a sin than a virtue，deemed(被认为是)后面跟的 a sin(罪)就是这些经理对诚实的定 性，评价性动词后的内容正是态度题答案信号。

analysis.label: 排除

questions.stem: What does the woman think is the priority of many managers?
questions.stemZh: 女士认为许多管理者的首要任务是什么?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: And retaining their power and prestige is their priority. 而且，保住他们的权力和威望，才是他们的首要之务。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 对话收尾处带 priority 的结论句。临近结束，女士用 And retaining their power and prestige is their priority 直接点出 priority，以 And 收束全段批评、给出结论，正是答案 信号——对话的总结判断落在这句。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: retaining their power and prestige ↔Preserving their power and prestige. retaining 换成 preserving，同义动词替换

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 未提及 原文说经理首要是保权保威，从没说他们以 Smoothing relationships in the workplace'维系职场关系'为先，这是凭好印象自造的目标，原文无对应。 B) 原词陷阱 原文多处用到 rational(如 They don't use the rational power of arguments)，B 的 Making rational and productive decisions'做理性高效决定'正是拿这个高频词设套；但全 篇批评经理不理性、靠话术保权，把'理性决策'当成他们的首要恰恰相反。 借用原文：They don't use the rational power of arguments to resolve issues C) 未提及 原文通篇批评经理只顾自己权威，绝无说他们以 Focusing on employees career growth'员工职业成长'为先，这与结论句的'保权'完全背离，原文无据。 Section B 1 Athletes are seen as heroes because they can do things that most of us can't do. They can hit fastballs coming at them at nearly 100 miles an hour, and leap and hang in the air, seemingly defying gravity. They get paid millions of dollars for their efforts, and their names and faces appear on everything from running shoes to advertising boards. 运动员被视为英雄，因为他们能做到我们大多数人做不到的事情。他们能击中以近100英里时速飞来的快 速球，能跳跃并悬停在空中，似乎在对抗地心引力。他们的努力为他们赢得了数百万美元的报酬，他们的 名字和面孔出现在从跑鞋到广告牌的各种事物上。 2 Athletes who are champions also show qualities such as perseverance, dedication, and the ability to keep their cool under pressure. Many show those same qualities off the playing field, too. Stories about superstar athletes teach us about working hard and believing in ourselves and then being passionate about what we do. Although it's usually bad behavior that gets an athlete a spot on the six o'clock news, many high-profile players work hard to be positive role models to children. They raise money for charities and act as mentors, talking to student groups and volunteering their time to programs that help children keep off drugs and stay in school. 成为冠军的运动员还展现出诸如毅力、奉献精神以及在压力下保持冷静的能力等品质。许多人在赛场外也 展现出同样的品质。关于超级明星运动员的故事教会我们努力工作、相信自己，然后对我们所做的事情充 满热情。尽管通常是不良行为让运动员登上六点钟新闻，但许多知名球员努力成为儿童的正面榜样。他们 为慈善事业筹款，担任导师，向学生团体演讲，并自愿将时间投入到帮助儿童远离毒品和留在学校的项 目中。 Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard. 3 Still, even the greatest champions have flaws. Just because an athlete has the perfect golf swing doesn't mean he is the perfect parent, friend or spokesperson. They also make mistakes. Separating an athlete's professional and personal lives can be tough. When a sports star gets in trouble with the law, or does something wrong in their private life, fans are often left disappointed. analysis.text: 开篇总起句直接定调。篇章第一句 weddings can get expensive 就是开门见山的总起，紧 接着 a few unexpected costs are bound to occur 进一步坐实"花费会超出预料"。开头总 起句是篇章题最常见的答案信号，听到第一句定性就该锁定。

analysis.text: a few unexpected costs are bound to occur ↔cost more than expected unexpected costs = cost more than expected

questions.stem: What did Susan's maid of honor advise her to do?

analysis.text: 建议信号 told her to。Her maid of honor told her to stick to the budget 中的 told her to 就是"建议"信号，信号后紧跟的动作 stick to the budget 即答案所在。听建议题， 认准 told sb to / advised 这类信号，落点就在其后的动词短语。

analysis.text: stick to the budget ↔Keep to her budget stick to = keep to

analysis.label: 定位

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 强否定动作 shut down + 理由。The bride quickly shut down the idea 里 shut down （直接否决）加上副词 quickly，语气强烈而干脆；后面 she did not want 的否定理由再次 坐实拒绝。态度题就抓这种强否定动作 + 否定理由作为信号。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: quickly shut down the idea ↔rejected it flatly quickly shut down = rejected flatly

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 与原文相反 She called it romantic.（说它浪漫）是正面反应，与原文 shut down the idea 的干脆否 决完全相反。原文里浪漫一词根本没出现，是凭"婚礼"联想出的诱选。 借用原文：The bride quickly shut down the idea B) 与原文相反 She welcomed it with open arms.（张开双臂欢迎）是强烈接受，恰与 Susan 的强烈拒绝 相对。这是把态度光谱拨到了相反一端的干扰。 借用原文：quickly shut down the idea C) 偷换概念 She said she would think about it.（说她会考虑）是夹在接受与拒绝之间的中间态度，最 像"温和版"答案。但原文是 quickly shut down——又快又决绝，没有任何"再想想"的余 地。把强否定弱化成"考虑"，是程度偷改。 借用原文：The bride quickly shut down the idea Section C 1 It has long been scientifically established that weather changes can affect people's moods. Now, a new study has provided evidence that temperature can influence people's personalities. This study of over 1.6 million people revealed that 22 degrees Celsius is the perfect air temperature to live in. A city with an average annual temperature closer to 22 tends to have a population who are more agreeable, conscientious, emotionally stable, and outgoing. It is the least taxing temperature for the body to regulate its own temperature. 长期以来,科学已经证实天气变化会影响人们的情绪。现在,一项新研究提供了证据表明温度可以影响人们 的性格。这项针对160多万人的研究显示,22摄氏度是最理想的生活气温。年平均气温接近22度的城市,其 人口往往更随和、更尽责、情绪更稳定、更外向。这是身体调节自身温度负担最小的温度。 2 The study was observational and didn't show cause and effect, but the scientists behind it theorized that better weather leads people to leave their home more often. This, in turn, leads to more social interaction, which encourages them to develop a friendlier and socially more acceptable personality. Warmer climates also make people feel more positive in general. They tend to be more agreeable and conscientious. 该研究是观察性的,并未显示因果关系,但背后的科学家们提出理论认为,更好的天气会导致人们更频繁地离 开家。这反过来又会带来更多的社交互动,从而鼓励他们发展出更友好、社会上更容易被接受的性格。更温 暖的气候也会让人们总体上感觉更积极。他们往往更随和、更尽责。 Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard. 3 The findings might help explain why colder and warmer countries tend to produce people with different personalities. Roughly speaking, about 40% of a person's personality is determined by their genes, the other 60% by their environment. It was already well-known that personality traits vary across geographic regions. Scientists also knew that these geographic personality traits are associated with a broad range of consequential outcomes. These outcomes include economic activity, for example, entrepreneurial start-up rates, and also crime rates, health behaviors, and health outcomes. 这些发现可能有助于解释为什么较冷和较暖的国家往往会培养出性格不同的人。大致来说,一个人的性格约 40%由基因决定,另外60%由环境决定。人们早已知道性格特征在不同地理区域之间存在差异。科学家们 也知道这些地理性格特征与一系列重要结果相关。这些结果包括经济活动,例如创业启动率,以及犯罪率、 健康行为和健康结果。 4 And it is well established that personality traits differ between countries. The research team speculated the two might be linked. To test this, they gave online personality tests to 5,587 Chinese students and 1.66 million Americans. They then compared the results with the average annual temperature where they grew up. The tests measured personality along five well-studied characteristics. The five were agreeability, conscientiousness, emotional stability, outgoingness, and openness to new experiences. In both groups, the researchers found the closer a town's average annual temperature was to 22 degrees, the more its population exhibited those personality characteristics. 性格特征在不同国家之间存在差异已是公认的事实。研究团队推测两者可能存在联系。为了验证这一点,他 们对5587名中国学生和166万美国人进行了在线性格测试。然后他们将结果与这些人成长地的年平均气温 进行比较。这些测试沿着五个经过充分研究的特征来衡量性格。这五个特征是随和性、尽责性、情绪稳定 性、外向性和对新体验的开放性。在两组人群中,研究人员发现,一个城镇的年平均气温越接近22度,其人口 就越表现出这些性格特征。 5 However, the findings were much stronger for the Chinese group than the Americans studied, which suggests that though temperature plays a role, it does not play a dominant role. The effects are fairly weak. It's unlikely to lead to many arguments over the temperature setting of the office air conditioner. 然而,这些发现在中国群体中比在所研究的美国人中要强得多,这表明虽然温度起作用,但它并不起主导作 用。这些影响相当微弱。它不太可能导致人们对办公室空调温度设置产生太多争论。

questions.stem: What has a new study revealed about temperature?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Now, a new study has provided evidence that temperature can influence people's personalities. 如今，一项新研究提供了证据，表明温度能够影响人的性格。

analysis.text: B) 与原文相反 B"人们尽管国籍不同却共享许多性格特质"，但原文 the findings were much stronger for the Chinese group than the Americans 恰恰强调中美两组结果差别很大（中国组强得 多），方向与"跨国籍相似"相反。 借用原文：the findings were much stronger for the Chinese group than the Americans studied C) 答非所问 C"同一地理区域的人性格可能不同"借用了原文 personality traits vary across geographic regions 关于地区差异的说法，但那是第三段的背景旧知识，且讲的是"跨地区"差异，不 是"测试 suggest"的结论；本题问 tests 说明了什么，答案在第五段的强弱定性，不在这 里。 借用原文：personality traits vary across geographic regions D) 原词陷阱 D"美国人显然比中国人更外向"盗用了原文测过的性格维度 outgoingness 和 Chinese/Americans 这些原词，但原文只说中国组的研究结果"更强"，从未比较两国谁更外 向；是把听过的词拼成一个原文没下的结论。 借用原文：outgoingness 1 Today, we are talking about loneliness. Loneliness and social isolation are growing public health concerns for people of all ages in the United States, from adolescence to the elderly. Public health experts are worried because loneliness seems to be on the rise, and studies have long found correlations between loneliness and an assortment of medical conditions that threaten health and longevity. 今天，我们要谈论孤独问题。孤独和社会隔离正在成为美国各年龄段人群日益关注的公共健康问题，从青 少年到老年人都受到影响。公共健康专家感到担忧，因为孤独似乎呈上升趋势，而且研究长期以来发现孤 独与威胁健康和寿命的各种医学状况之间存在关联。 2 The problem of loneliness may be even greater than we thought. A new national poll found that about a third of older Americans are lonely, and almost as many seniors feel isolated. This is a serious problem as research shows that chronic loneliness is particularly harmful to senior citizens. That's because it can impair older adults' memory and damage their physical and mental health. Chronic loneliness even impacts the life expectancy of seniors, increasing their risk of early mortality. 孤独问题可能比我们想象的更严重。一项新的全国性民意调查发现，约三分之一的美国老年人感到孤独， 几乎同样多的老年人感到孤立。这是一个严重的问题，因为研究表明慢性孤独对老年人尤其有害。这是因 为它会损害老年人的记忆力，损害他们的身心健康。慢性孤独甚至影响老年人的预期寿命，增加他们早逝 的风险。 Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard. 3 Let's take a closer look at that poll now. More than a third of seniors in the poll said they felt lonely at least some of the time, and 27% said they sometimes or often felt isolated. This reflects how much time the seniors spent with others. Almost 30% said they socialized with friends, family or neighbors once a week or less. Women were more likely than men to report loneliness. 现在让我们仔细看看这项民意调查。调查中超过三分之一的老年人表示他们至少有时感到孤独，27%的人 表示有时或经常感到孤立。这反映了老年人与他人相处的时间。近30%的人表示他们每周与朋友、家人或 邻居社交一次或更少。女性比男性更容易报告感到孤独。 4 But there is good news. It looks like loneliness can be reversed. But researchers are still trying to determine the best way to do so. Why is that? Resolving the problem of loneliness among seniors often isn't as simple as getting them together with others or moving them in with their children. In fact, the poll found that seniors who lived with their children were more likely to report feeling lonely than those who didn't. This may be because loneliness refers to the discrepancy between actual and desired relationships. So it's possible that someone who lives alone doesn't meet that definition, while someone in a house full of busy people does. 但也有好消息。看起来孤独是可以逆转的。但研究人员仍在试图确定最佳方法。为什么呢？解决老年人孤 独问题往往并不像让他们与他人聚在一起或让他们与子女同住那么简单。事实上，调查发现与子女同住的 老年人比不与子女同住的老年人更容易报告感到孤独。这可能是因为孤独指的是实际关系与期望关系之间 的差异。因此，独居的人可能不符合这个定义，而住在满是忙碌人群的房子里的人却符合。 5 How can we solve the problem? Well, the researchers assert that it's important to address each person's underlying cause of loneliness, whether it's the death of a spouse, medical problems, or social expectations that haven't been fulfilled. It's noteworthy that there is one general recommendation. While finding solutions for loneliness is highly personal, research suggests the best interventions are those that involve meaningful social contact at least once a week. Depending on the person, that could mean volunteering, seeing an old friend or something else. 我们如何解决这个问题？研究人员断言，重要的是要解决每个人孤独的根本原因，无论是配偶的去世、医 疗问题，还是未实现的社会期望。值得注意的是，有一个总体建议。虽然寻找孤独的解决方案是高度个人 化的，但研究表明最好的干预措施是那些涉及每周至少一次有意义的社交接触的措施。根据个人情况，这 可能意味着做志愿者、拜访老朋友或其他活动。

A) The fog still chills the morning air and the cable cars still climb halfway to the stars. Yet on the ground, the Bay area has changed greatly since singer Tony Bennett left his heart here. Silicon Valley and the tech industry have led the region into a period of unprecedented wealth and innovation. But existing political and land limits have caused an alarming housing crisis and astronomical rise in social and economic difference.
B) While the residents of most cities display pride and support for their home industries, drastic market distortions in the San Francisco Bay Area have created boiling resentment in the region towards the tech industry. A vocal minority is even calling on officials to punish those who are benefitting from the economic and housing boom. If this boom and its consequences are not resolved, a drastic increase in social and economic difference may have a profound impact on the region for generations. A history and analysis of this transformation may hold invaluable insights about the opportunities. Perils of tech cities are currently being cultivated across the US, and indeed around the world.
C) According to a recent study, San Francisco ranks first in California for economic difference. The average income of the top 1% of households in the city averages $3.6 million. This is 44 times the average income of those at the bottom, which stands at $81,094. The top 1% of the San Francisco peninsula's share of total income now extends to 30.8% of the region's income. This was a dramatic jump from 1989, where it stood at 15.8%.
D) The region's economy has been fundamentally transformed by the technology industry springing from Silicon Valley. Policies pushed by Mayor Ed Lee provided tax breaks for tech companies to set up shop along the city's long-neglected Mid-Market area. The city is now home to Twitter, Uber, Airbnb, Pinterest, Dropbox and others. In short, the Bay Area has become a global magnet for those with specialized skills, which has in turn helped fuel economic enthusiasm, and this economic growth has reduced unemployment to 3.4%, an admirable feat.
E) In spite of all that, the strength of the recent job growth, combined with policies that have traditionally limited housing development in the city and throughout the peninsula, did not help ease the affordability crisis. In 2015 alone, the Bay Area added 64,000 in jobs. In the same year, only 5,000 new homes were built.
F) With the average house in the city costing over $1.25 million and average flat prices over $1.11 million, the minimum qualifying income to purchase a house has increased to $254,000. Considering that the average household income in the city currently stands at around $80,000, it is not an exaggeration to say that the dream of home ownership is now beyond the grasp of the vast majority of today's people who rent.
G) For generations, the stability and prosperity of the American middle class have been anchored by home ownership. Studies have consistently shown that the value of land has overtaken overall income growth, thus providing a huge advantage to property owners as a vehicle of wealth building. When home prices soar above the reach of most households, the gap between the rich and the poor dramatically increases.
H) If contributing factors leading to housing becoming less than affordable are not resolved over multiple generations, a small elite will control a vast share of the country's total wealth. The result? A society where the threat of class warfare would loom large. A society's level of happiness is tied less to measures of quantitative wealth and more to measures of qualitative wealth. This means that how a person judges their security in comparison to their neighbors' has more of an impact on their happiness than their objective standard of living. At the same time, when a system no longer provides opportunities for the majority to participate in wealth building, it not only robs those who are excluded from opportunities, but also deprives them of their dignity.
I) San Francisco and the Bay Area have long been committed to values which embrace inclusion and rejection of mainstream culture. To see these values coming apart so publicly adds insult to injury for a region once defined by its progressive social fabric. In the face of resentment, it is human to want revenge. But deteriorating policies such as heavily taxing technology companies or real estate developers are not likely to shift the balance.
J) The housing crisis is caused by two primary factors: the growing desirability of the Bay Area as a place to live due to its excellent economy, and our limited housing stock. Although the city is experiencing an unprecedented boom in new housing, more units are sorely needed. Protection policies were originally designed to suppress bad development and boost historic preservation in our urban areas. Now, too many developers are experiencing excessive delays. Meanwhile, there are the land limitations of the Bay Area to consider. The region is surrounded by water and mountains. Local governments need to aid development as well. This means increasing housing density throughout the region and building upwards while streamlining the approval process.
K) Real estate alone will not solve the problem, of course. Transportation, too, needs to be updated and infrastructure extended to link distant regions to Silicon Valley and the city. We need to build an effective high-speed commuting system linking the high-priced and crowded Bay Area with the low- priced and low-density Central Valley. This would dramatically reduce travel times. And based on the operating speeds of hovering trains used in countries such as Japan or Spain, high-speed rail could shorten the time to travel between San Francisco and California's capital, Sacramento, or from Stockton to San Jose, to under 30 minutes. This system would bring once distant regions within reasonable commute to heavy job centers. The city also needs to update existing transportation routes combined with smart home-building policies that dramatically increase housing density in areas surrounding high-speed rail stations. By doing so, we will be able to build affordable housing within acceptable commuting distances for a significant bulk of the workforce.
L) Our threatening housing crisis forces the difficult question of what type of society we would like to be. Will it be one where the elite command the vast bulk of wealth and regional culture is defined by an aggressive business world? We were recently treated to a taste of the latter, when local tech employee Justin Keller wrote an open letter to the city complaining about having to see homeless people on his way to work.
M) It doesn't have to be this way. But solutions need to be implemented now, before angry crowds grow from a nuisance to serious concern. It may take less than you might think. And in fact, the solutions to our housing crisis are already fairly clear. We need to increase the density of housing units. We need to use existing technology to shorten travel times and break the land limits. There is a way to solve complex social and economic problems without abandoning social responsibility. This is the Bay Area's opportunity to prove that it can innovate more than just technology. 36. The higher rate of employment, combined with limited housing supply, did not make it any easier to buy a house.

P1 The ability to make inferences from same and different, once thought to be unique to humans, is viewed as a cornerstone of abstract intelligent thought. A new study, however, has shown that what psychologists call same-different discrimination is present in creatures generally seen as unintelligent: newborn ducklings(小鸭).

P2 The study, published Thursday in Science, challenges our idea of what it means to have a birdbrain, said Edward Wasserman, an experimental psychologist at the University of Iowa who wrote an independent review of the study.

P3 "In fact, birds are extremely intelligent and our problem pretty much lies in figuring out how to get them to 'talk' to us, or tell us how smart they really are," he said.

P4 Antone Martinho and Alex Kacelnik, co-authors of the new paper, devised a clever experiment to better test bird intelligence.

P5 First, they took 1-day-old ducklings and exposed them to a pair of moving objects. The two objects were either the same or different in shape or color. Then they exposed each duckling to two entirely new pairs of moving objects.

P6 The researchers found that about 70% of the ducklings preferred to move toward the pair of objects that had the same shape or color relationship as the first objects they saw. A duckling that was first shown two green spheres, in other words, was more likely to move toward a pair of blue spheres than a mismatched pair of orange and purple spheres.

P7 Ducklings go through a rapid learning process called imprinting shortly after birth—it's what allows them to identify and follow their mothers.

P8 These findings suggest that ducklings use abstract relationships between sensory inputs like color, shape, sounds and odor to recognize their mothers, said Dr. Kacelnik.

P9 By studying imprinting, the authors of this study have shown for the first time that an animal can learn relationships between concepts without training, said Jeffrey Katz, an experimental psychologist at Auburn University who was not involved in the study.

P10 Previous studies have suggested that other animals, including pigeons, dolphins, honeybees and some primates(灵长类动物), can discern same from different, but only after extensive training.

P11 Adding ducklings to the list—particularly untrained newborn ducklings—suggests that the ability to compare abstract concepts "is far more necessary to a wider variety of animals' survival than we previously thought," Dr. Martinho said. He believes the ability is so crucial because it helps animals consider context when identifying objects in their environment.

P12 It's clear from this study and others like it that "animals process and appreciate far more of the intricacies in their world than we've ever understood," Dr. Wasserman said. "We are in a revolutionary phase in terms of our ability to understand the minds of other animals."

blocks.text: Adding ducklings to the list—particularly untrained newborn ducklings—suggests that the ability to compare abstract concepts "is far more necessary to a wider variety of animals' survival than we previously thought," Dr. Martinho said. P1 The suggestion that people should aim for dietary diversity by trying to eat a variety of foods has been a basic public health recommendation for decades in the United States and elsewhere. Now, however, experts are warning that aiming for a diverse diet may actually lead to just eating more calories, and, thus, to obesity. One issue is that people may not interpret "variety" the way nutritionists intend. This problem is highlighted by new research conducted by the American Heart Association. Researchers reviewed all the evidence published related to dietary diversity and saw a correlation between dietary diversity and a greater intake of both healthy and unhealthy foods. This had implications for obesity, as researchers found a greater prevalence of obesity amongst people with a greater dietary diversity.

P2 One author of the new study explained that their findings contradict standard dietary advice, as most dietary guidelines around the world include a statement of eating a variety of foods. But this advice does not seem to be supported by science, possibly because there is little agreement about the meaning of "dietary diversity," which is not clearly and consistently defined. Some experts measure dietary diversity by counting the number of food groups eaten, while others look at the distribution of calories across individual foods, and still others measure how different the foods eaten are from each other.

P3 Although the findings of this new study contradict standard dietary advice, they do not come as a surprise to all of the researchers involved. Dr. Rao, one of the study authors, noted that, after 20 years of experience in the field of obesity, he has observed that people who have a regimented lifestyle and diet tend to be thinner and healthier than people with a wide variety of consumption. This anecdotal evidence matches the conclusions of the study, which found no evidence that dietary diversity promotes healthy body weight or optimal eating patterns, and limited evidence that eating a variety of foods is actually associated with consuming more calories, poor eating patterns and weight gain. Further, there is some evidence that a greater variety of food options in a single meal may delay people's feeling of fullness and actually increase how much they eat.

P4 Based on their findings, the researchers endorse a diet consisting of a limited number of healthy foods such as vegetables, fruits, grains, and poultry. They also recommend that people simultaneously endeavor to restrict consumption of sweets, sugar and red meat. The researchers stress, however, that their dietary recommendations do not imply dietary diversity is never positive, and that, in the past, diversity in diets of whole, unprocessed food may have actually been very beneficial. 51. What has been a standard piece of dietary advice for decades? A) People should cultivate a healthy eating habit. B) People should have a well-balanced diet. C) People should diversify what they eat. D) People should limit calorie intake to avoid obesity.

writing.directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence “People are now increasingly aware of the danger of ‘appearance anxiety’ or being obsessed with one’s looks.” You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
writing.model: People are now increasingly aware of the danger of ‘appearance anxiety’ or being obsessed with one’s looks. This uneasiness rarely appears out of nowhere. Bombarded daily by filtered images and narrow aesthetic standards on social media, many young people measure themselves against unreachable models and feel that they never look good enough. The constant comparison quietly drains their confidence and even distracts them from things that truly matter. Yet a healthier attitude is well within our reach. The key is to shift attention from the mirror to inner value — our knowledge, kindness and abilities. I once spent hours worrying about a small scar before a presentation, until a friend reminded me that the audience remembered my ideas, not my face. That moment taught me that self-acceptance, rather than a flawless appearance, is what sets us free. In short, looks are only a thin surface of who we are. Once we learn to value character over appearance, ‘appearance anxiety’ loses its grip, and we can live with genuine confidence.

translation.reference: Zhang Qian was the first great explorer in Chinese history. Braving dangers and overcoming numerous difficulties, he made two journeys to the Western Regions, opened up trade between China, West Asia and Europe, transported Chinese silk and silk fabrics there, and thereby pioneered the famous Silk Road in history. sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: Zhang Qian was explorer（主系表）（主语策略：原句主语） 这是"A是B"的判断句，主语用原句已有的 张骞(Zhang Qian)，谓语用系动词 was，表语是 the first great explorer。主干即 Zhang Qian was the first great explorer，再把"中国"挂上去说明 范围。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: "中国第一个伟大的"全作前置定语 本句很短、结构简单，无需降级成从句。"第一个""伟大的"是形容词，按英文习惯叠在名词 explorer 前作前置定语：the first great explorer；"中国（的）"表范围，可处理成 in China 后 置，或 in Chinese history，挂在 explorer 之后，避免一串修饰全压在名词前显得拥挤。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 回指全篇基调用一般过去时，系动词用 was（张骞是古人，不是 is）。 冠词与序数词 序数词 first 前必须加定冠词 the：the first great explorer；漏掉 the 是高频硬伤。 单复数 explorer 此处特指张骞一人，用单数。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: Zhang Qian was the first great explorer in Chinese history. 2. 他不畏艰险,克服重重困难,两次出使西域,开通了中国同西亚和欧洲的通商关系,将中国的丝和 丝织品运往西亚和欧洲,开拓了历史上著名的"丝绸之路"。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: He + 一串并列谓语（主语策略：原句主语） 本句一个主语 他（指张骞）贯穿到底，后面跟着"不畏""克服""出使""开通""运往""开拓"一连串动 作。骨架定为 He, ..., made two trips / journeys to the Western Regions，把"两次出使西域"这 个核心壮举作为主干谓语，其余分句分别降级或并列安放，避免六个动词全用 and 平铺。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 前提降级为分词、成就拆成并列分句 "不畏艰险，克服重重困难"是出使的前提条件，降级成现在分词短语 Braving dangers and overcoming numerous difficulties 作状语，置于句首。"开通了……通商关系""将丝和丝织品运 往……""开拓了丝绸之路"是出使带来的几项成就，因信息量大，拆成主干之后用分号或 thereby + 分词连接的并列结构：he opened up trade between China and West Asia and Europe, transported Chinese silk and silk fabrics there, and pioneered the famous Silk Road，用一 个 and 串起的并列谓语收束，避免写成六段流水。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 回指全篇基调用一般过去时：made / opened / transported / pioneered 全用过去式。 单复数 "丝织品"是多种、用复数 silk fabrics；"困难"重重、用复数 difficulties；"两次"出使 made two journeys 用复数 journeys。 介词搭配 "开通……通商关系"用 open up trade between A and B；"运往"用 transport ... to ... 或承前用 there；"出使（前往）西域"用 to。 专名统一 "西域"= the Western Regions、"丝绸之路"= the Silk Road，回指 glossary、加定冠词大写。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: Braving dangers and overcoming numerous difficulties, he made two journeys to the Western Regions, opened up trade between China, West Asia and Europe, transported Chinese silk and silk fabrics there, and thereby pioneered the famous Silk Road in history. 3. 同时,他又将西域的风土人情、地理文化以及特有物种等介绍到中原,极大地开阔了人们的 视野。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: He introduced ... to the Central Plains（主语策略：原句主语） 主语仍是 他（he），核心动词"介绍到"作谓语 introduced，宾语是"西域的风土人情、地理文化以 及特有物种"，地点状语"到中原"= to the Central Plains。主干即 he introduced the customs, geography, culture and unique species of the Western Regions to the Central Plains。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: "极大地开阔视野"降级为结果状语 句首 同时 译为 Meanwhile/At the same time 作连接状语。后半句"极大地开阔了人们的视 野"是"介绍"带来的结果，不另起一句，降级成现在分词短语 greatly broadening people’s horizons 作结果状语挂在主干后；并列的几个宾语（风土人情、地理文化、特有物种）用 and 连 成名词并列，共一个 of the Western Regions 收尾。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 回指全篇基调用一般过去时：introduced 用过去式。 单复数 "特有物种"不止一种、用复数 species（单复同形，但配 unique 取复数义）；"人们的视野"用 people’s horizons，horizon 在"眼界"义上常用复数。 专名统一 "西域"=the Western Regions、"中原"=the Central Plains，回指 glossary、加定冠词大写。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: Meanwhile, he introduced the local customs, geography, culture and unique species of the Western Regions to the Central Plains, greatly broadening people's horizons. 4. 正如历史学家所指出的那样,如果没有张骞出使西域,就不可能有丝绸之路的开辟,也就不会有汉 朝同西域或欧洲的文化交流。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: There would have been no ...（虚拟存在句）（主语策略：There be） "就不可能有……开辟""也就不会有……交流"都是"（不会）存在某事物"，用 There be 句型表存 在最贴切；又因是与过去事实相反的假设（如果没有张骞出使西域），主句用虚拟语气 There would have been no...。前面 正如历史学家所指出的那样 作插入状语 As historians have pointed out。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 条件句 + 两个并列 no 结果 "如果没有张骞出使西域"是条件从句，与过去相反，用 Without Zhang Qian’s mission to the Western Regions 介词短语表条件（比 If there had been no... 更简洁），或 Had it not been for...。两个结果分句"不可能有丝绸之路开辟""不会有文化交流"是并列，合进一个 There would have been no A, nor B 结构，用 nor 承接第二个否定，避免重复 there would have been no。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 虚拟语气 与过去事实相反，主句用 would have + 过去分词（would have been），不能用一般过去时 was/were；这是本句最易错也最显水平处。 时态（插入语） "历史学家所指出的"是延续到现在的评价，用现在完成时 have pointed out，可不必受全篇过去时 基调约束。 专名统一 "西域"=the Western Regions、"丝绸之路"=the Silk Road、"汉朝"=the Han Dynasty，回指 glossary。 单复数 "历史学家"泛指一类人、用复数 historians；"文化交流"用 cultural exchanges（交流多次、用复 数）。
